intro: Manaccan is a village on the Lizard side of the Helford River in Cornwall, and the creeks below it run into some of the mildest, most sheltered woodland in England. In the village itself a fig at least 200 years old grows straight out of the twelfth-century south wall of the parish church. Down near the hamlet of Carne a Monterey cypress leans out over the water from the creek path, its long limbs framing the tide, with a bench beside it.
meta_description: A fig growing out of Manaccan's church wall for at least 200 years, and a Monterey cypress over a tidal creek near Carne, on the Helford River in Cornwall.

trees.name: The Monterey Cypress over the Creek

location.address: Creekside path near Carne, Manaccan, Helford River, Cornwall

trees.story:
A reader walking a path above a tidal creek near Carne, on the Lizard side of the Helford River, called this "a spectacular tree hanging over the creek" and added that there is a lovely bench to sit and ponder. Both halves of that are easy to believe.

The trunk flares into deep, fluted buttresses at the base and rises in long vertical ridges of grey-brown bark. Several heavy limbs run out horizontally over the water, and a few of them end in old pruning cuts where the tree has been kept clear of the path. Above them the crown is dense and dark green.

The Monterey cypress comes from a pair of small groves on the California coast, yet in the mild, salt-laden air of Cornwall it grows fast and large and has become part of the creek-side landscape. We have no measurement or age for this one, so we do not guess at either. The photograph is a reader's, and the pin is their GPS fix at the tree.
trees.how_to_recognise: A big Monterey cypress with a fluted, buttressed trunk and long horizontal limbs reaching out over a tidal creek, a bench beside it.
verified_sources: A reader's photographs and note through the app, 2026-11-15, with a GPS fix at the tree
trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-15: sent by a reader through the app, species given as Monterey Cypress, note 'Spectacular tree hanging over the creek, lovely bench to sit and ponder', no age or girth. Both photographs viewed: a large old Monterey cypress, fluted buttress base, heavy horizontal limbs with a few cut stubs over tidal water, daylight, whole tree. Place: OSM reverse geocode of the fix gives the hamlet of Carne in the parish of Manaccan, on the Lizard side of the Helford River; the creek itself is not named in any source we read. No register entry within 100 m (the Woodland Trust Ancient Tree Inventory's Falmouth-area Monterey cypress records are not at this spot). No age, no girth. Pin: reader's GPS fix, confirmed.
trees.access: Free, from a public creekside path near Carne; a bench stands beside it. Check the tide and keep to the path.

trees.name: The Fig in Manaccan Church Wall
trees.age_estimate: at least 200 years by the parish's account; 200 to 400 by a reader's estimate

location.address: Church of St Manaccus and St Dunstan, Vicarage Lane, Manaccan, Cornwall

trees.story:
A fig tree has been growing out of the wall of Manaccan's church for at least 200 years, and nobody knows how it got there. Historic England's listing of the building mentions it in passing. The lower part of the south wall is twelfth-century work, and "from the left-hand corner grows a very old fig tree".

The church of St Manaccus and St Dunstan is Grade I listed and far older than its fig. The village first appears in a charter of King Edgar in 960, and the tower went up in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries. A gardening writer who went to look explained how a tree can live in a wall at all. The wall is two faces of stone with rubble packed between them, and the roots have found their way into that core.

The reader who sent us its photographs puts it at 200 to 400 years old, by their estimate. In their words, "The old fig tree is growing out of the walls of Manaccan Church." Their pictures show a gnarled, knuckled base wedged into the masonry above head height, where the south wall meets the tower, and a thicket of grey stems carrying a dome of big lobed leaves against the old stone. It is free to see from the churchyard.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the dome of big lobed fig leaves sprouting from the stonework above head height. It grows out of the church's south wall, at the corner where the wall meets the tower.
verified_sources: A reader's photographs and note through the app, 2026-11-15, with a GPS fix at the tree
trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-15 session (c): sent by a reader through the app as Common Fig, age '200 to 400', four photographs; their later note (submission): 'The old fig tree is growing out of the walls of Manaccan Church'. Wikipedia (citing Cornwall Online Parish Clerks): a fig at least 200 years old grows out of the western part of the south wall; charter of King Edgar 960; tower 14th to 15th century; Grade I. Historic England listing: lower south wall C12, 'from the left-hand corner grows a very old fig tree'. roys-roy blog 2013: wall of two faces with rubble core, origin unknown. Photographs viewed: fig rooted in the masonry at the junction of the south wall and the tower, crown of lobed leaves, daylight. Pin: the reader's GPS fix, kept and confirmed. OSM's outline of the church (way 158587050) runs 50.08312 to 50.08333 N, -5.12724 to -5.12690 E; the fix sits a few metres off its south-west corner, which is where the south wall meets the tower and where Wikipedia and the photographs put the fig. The reader's later hand-moved pin (50.083246, -5.126540) lands about 25 m east of the church's east end, off the building, so it was not used. An earlier hold (shrub-sized, no age source) is answered by the listing and parish sources. 2026-11-17 reader judge: pin moved 55 m on reader report 1000029; confirmed.
trees.access: Free, from the churchyard of the parish church.

question_meta: The Monterey cypress over the creek near Carne, Manaccan, on the Helford River: what it looks like and where it stands.
question_answer: It is a large Monterey cypress growing at the edge of a tidal creek near Carne, in the parish of Manaccan on the Helford River in Cornwall. Its limbs reach out over the water, and a bench stands beside it. We have no age for it.
question_context: A reader found this tree on the creek path near Carne and sent photographs with a GPS fix. The trunk flares into fluted buttresses and several heavy limbs run out horizontally over the water. The Monterey cypress is native to two small groves on the California coast and grows large in Cornwall's mild air. We have no measurement or age for this tree. Several of its limbs end in old pruning cuts, where it has been kept clear of the path. In the reader's words it is a spectacular tree hanging over the creek, with a lovely bench to sit and ponder. The place is the hamlet of Carne, in the parish of Manaccan, a village on the Lizard side of the Helford River. The creek itself is not named in any source we found, so the page names the hamlet and leaves the creek unnamed. The pin is the reader's GPS fix taken at the trunk.

faq.a: On the creek path near Carne, in the parish of Manaccan, on the Lizard side of the Helford River.
We do not know. No source we found gives an age or a measurement.

faq.q: Is there really a tree growing out of Manaccan church?
faq.a: Yes. A fig at least 200 years old grows out of the south wall, at the corner by the tower, and can be seen free from the churchyard.
